title: Personal Checking: Courtesy Refund Allowances by Tier
content:
Goodwill (courtesy) refunds of correctly assessed Personal Checking fees are rationed by tier in two ways: how many one customer may receive in any rolling 365-day window, and how many calendar days after a fee posts it remains eligible.

| Tier | Courtesy refunds per rolling 365 days | Days after posting a fee stays eligible |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Student Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Everyday Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Interest Checking | 2 | 60 |
| Premier Checking | 3 | 90 |
| Private Client Checking | 6 | 120 |

## How the figures are counted

- The yearly figure counts refunded fees, one per fee, across every checking account the customer holds, not per account.
- The day figure is a count of calendar days since the fee posted; a fee is eligible only while no more than that many days have gone by.

## Quick answers

- A Private Client Checking customer may receive up to six courtesy refunds in a rolling year; an Everyday Checking customer, one.
- A fee on a Premier Checking account that posted 90 calendar days ago is still within its window; at 91 days it is outside.
